001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007/**
008 * Written once for each signed request the pump receives on the CONTROL characteristic.
009 *
010 * <p>The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum
011 * do not name this opcode.
012 *
013 * <p>In Trio/TandemKit logs these records match the {@code Writing message} lines one to one in
014 * both directions: every record had a request with the same opcode within 30 seconds (3891/3891
015 * records from the maintainer's Mobi, 1358/1360 from a tester's Mobi), and every such request
016 * written while the pump's history was being fetched produced one. The pump writes the record
017 * after the effect of the command, so a stop/set temp rate cycle reads TempRateCompleted, this
018 * record (StopTempRate), {@link ControlResponseHistoryLog}, TempRateActivated, this record
019 * (SetTempRate), {@link SetTempRateResponseHistoryLog}.
020 *
021 * <p>Bolus-flow requests (BolusPermission, InitiateBolus, CancelBolus, BolusPermissionRelease,
022 * RemoteBgEntry, RemoteCarbEntry) do not produce this record; their trailer time shows up in
023 * other, bolus-specific records instead.
024 *
025 * <p>Bytes 15-25 were zero in all 7447 records examined. See
026 * https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/145.
027 */
028@HistoryLogProps(
029    opCode = 290,
030    displayName = "Control Request",
031    internalName = ""
032)
033public class ControlRequestHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
034
035    private long requestTimestamp;
036    private int requestOpCode;
037
038    public ControlRequestHistoryLog() {}
039    public ControlRequestHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long requestTimestamp, int requestOpCode) {
040        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
041        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, requestTimestamp, requestOpCode);
042        this.requestTimestamp = requestTimestamp;
043        this.requestOpCode = requestOpCode;
044    }
045
046    public ControlRequestHistoryLog(long requestTimestamp, int requestOpCode) {
047        this(0, 0, requestTimestamp, requestOpCode);
048    }
049
050    public int typeId() {
051        return 290;
052    }
053
054    /**
055     * <table border="1">
056     * <caption>Parsed fields for ControlRequestHistoryLog:</caption>
057     * <tr><td><code>requestTimestamp</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10)</code></td></tr>
058     * <tr><td><code>requestOpCode</code></td><td><code>raw[14] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
059     * </table>
060     */
061    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
062        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
063        this.cargo = raw;
064        parseBase(raw);
065        this.requestTimestamp = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10);
066        this.requestOpCode = raw[14] & 0xFF;
067    }
068
069    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long requestTimestamp, int requestOpCode) {
070        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
071            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(290, 0),
072            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
073            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
074            Bytes.toUint32(requestTimestamp),
075            new byte[]{ (byte) requestOpCode }));
076    }
077
078    /**
079     * The 4-byte time value carried in the signed request's 24-byte trailer (the 4 bytes before
080     * the HMAC), copied as the app sent it. This is not a pump clock reading.
081     *
082     * <p>pumpX2 and TandemKit fill that field with {@code PumpStateSupplier.pumpTimeSinceReset},
083     * so with them it equals the most recent {@code TimeSinceResetResponse.pumpTimeSinceReset}
084     * the app had received (3889/3891 and 1358/1360 records on two Mobi pumps; the misses fall in
085     * gaps of the app log). That is why it can lag the record's own time by minutes. Tandem's
086     * official app fills it with the phone's UTC time in seconds since 2008-01-01, so there it
087     * differs from the record's pump-local time by the time-zone offset.
088     *
089     * <p>In the official-app BLE captures the pair (this value, {@link #getRequestOpCode()})
090     * equalled the trailer time and opcode of a captured signed CONTROL request for 482 records
091     * on six pumps.
092     *
093     * @return the request's signed trailer time value
094     */
095    public long getRequestTimestamp() {
096        return requestTimestamp;
097    }
098
099    /**
100     * The request's opcode as an unsigned byte, i.e. the pumpX2 {@code opCode} of the request
101     * message ANDed with 0xFF: for example 164 is SetTempRateRequest (opCode -92), 166 is
102     * StopTempRateRequest (-90), 184 is DismissNotificationRequest (-72), 148 is
103     * EnterFillTubingModeRequest (-108) and 132 is UserInteractionRequest (-124).
104     *
105     * @return the unsigned opcode of the signed CONTROL request that was received
106     */
107    public int getRequestOpCode() {
108        return requestOpCode;
109    }
110}
